Definition: perhaps from πράσον (a leek, and so an onion-patch); a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement):--in ranks.
BiblicalUsage: Prasia is a garden plot, a bed, and Mark uses it once for the feeding of the five thousand. The people sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties, in garden beds across the grass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the order of those beds shows a God who feeds thousands without confusion, and no one goes hungry at his table.
